title: Post-beta tuning backlog + expansion plan for tiered batching defaults
creator: Talia Benson
body:
Context
- This is the follow-up work item after the limited beta rollout of tiered batching defaults (fast / standard / cost-efficient).
- Goal: consolidate learnings, turn them into a parameter tuning backlog (scoped by model family + GPU SKU), and define a safe expansion plan to additional regions/models.

Links / artifacts
- Parameter sweep results: google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/tiered-batching-parameter-sweep-results-v1.json
- Rollout checklist (living): google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/batching-defaults-rollout-checklist.json
- Queue delay calibration notes: google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/scheduler-notes-queue-delay-calibration.json
- Related PRs (already merged in beta window):
  - PR 18463 (streaming cadence regression fix)
  - PR 18488 (overload protection alignment w/ cost-efficient)
  - PR 18515 (canary rollout tooling)
  - PR 18539 (KV cache pressure edge-case)
- Support signal to incorporate: SUP-18492 (timeouts on cost-efficient), SUP-18510 (confusion about tier vs explicit overrides), INT-3301 (request for troubleshooting playbook)

Beta learnings (what we saw)
1) Streaming sensitivity is higher than expected (fast tier)
- Issue: token cadence and first-token latency were impacted when max_queue_delay was non-zero under moderate concurrency; decode prioritization also mattered.
- Outcome: shipped a decode prioritization tweak + regression test (PR 18463). Still need per-model tuning because prefill/decode ratio changes with architecture/context.

2) Cost-efficient tier can trigger overload protection earlier on smaller memory SKUs
- Symptom: a subset of customers saw increased timeouts/5xx when cost-efficient was enabled at high concurrency.
- Root cause hypothesis (from canary + repro): KV cache pressure + longer queue delay increased in-flight memory footprint; overload protection shed later than ideal, causing tail latency spikes.
- Outcome: added guardrails + backpressure reason codes (PR 18488) and adjusted KV cache thresholds (PR 18539). Remaining work: SKU-specific defaults (A10/L4/L40S especially) and clearer customer guidance.

3) “One standard tier” is not enough across GPU SKUs
- H100: can sustain larger effective batches with minimal p95 penalty; default max_batch and queue delay can be more aggressive.
- A100: moderate batching works but queue delay must be bounded tightly for streaming routes.
- L40S/A10/L4 class: memory pressure becomes the dominant constraint at higher concurrency; batching must be capped by KV cache budget more than queue delay.

4) Customers want to understand effective behavior
- Repeated request: “what did the tier actually set?” and “which explicit override is winning?”
- Outcome: config explain endpoint (PR 18470) helps, but we need to standardize what gets logged/returned and add a short troubleshooting flow (ties to INT-3301).

5) Model-family differences that materially affect best defaults
- Long-context variants (e.g., 32k/128k) need stricter prefill admission control / KV cache budgeting.
- Quantized variants shift the trade-off: better throughput at same batch size, but can cause different saturation points and queueing behavior.

Tuning backlog (by model family x GPU SKU)
A) Streaming routes (chat/completions with stream=true)
- Owners: Sofia Ivanova + Marcus Reed
- Work:
  - Re-run streaming cadence checks for fast tier across top 5 models in beta (per region) at concurrency sweep {1, 4, 8, 16, 32}.
  - Tighten fast-tier queue delay for streaming: propose max_queue_delay_ms = 0–2ms target range depending on SKU.
  - Add a gating metric: “stream inter-token gap p95” and fail canary if regression > 10% vs baseline.

B) Cost-efficient defaults on memory-constrained SKUs
- Owners: Omar El-Sayed + Yuki Sato
- Work:
  - Add SKU overrides for KV cache pressure limits and max_batch caps (L40S/A10/L4).
  - Ensure overload protection triggers earlier (load shed) rather than letting queueing accumulate; verify error rates don’t rise.
  - Add a canary scenario explicitly targeting OOM-near conditions (high concurrency, medium prompts, long generation) to validate stability.

C) Long-context model overrides
- Owners: Lena Fischer + Arjun Desai
- Work:
  - Define “long-context” profile rule in tier mapping (context window >= 32k) and apply stricter admission control / batch caps.
  - Validate that standard tier meets p95 targets for 8k/32k prompts while keeping GPU util reasonable.

D) Region-specific calibration
- Owners: Rafael Mendes + Julian Moore
- Work:
  - Confirm queue delay metrics are comparable across regions (clock skew / ingestion delays) and update dashboards if needed.
  - Validate network variance is not being misattributed to scheduler queueing (dashboards should split server-side vs client-perceived latency where possible).

Expansion plan (models + regions)
Phase 1: Expand regions for existing beta models (safe)
- Regions: add eu-west-1 after us-east-1/us-west-2 are stable; then ap-southeast-1.
- Default enablement: keep behind tiered rollout tooling (PR 18515) with per-region percentage ramps.
- Ramp schedule (suggested): 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% per region with a 24h hold between steps.

Phase 2: Expand models in existing regions (moderate)
- Add next tranche of models (top usage + representative architectures):
  - One “heavy prefill” model, one “decode heavy” model, one long-context model, one quantized variant.
- Require: perf canary coverage added for each new model/SKU combination before increasing beyond 25%.

Phase 3: Make standard tier default for selected routes (high impact)
- Only after:
  - Standard tier holds p95 and error rate SLO for 2 weeks on 100% traffic for Phase 1/2 coverage.
  - Support playbook and docs are updated (INT-3301 closure criteria).

Abort / rollback signals (must be wired to rollout checklist)
- p95 server-side latency regression > 15% vs baseline for the same model/SKU/route over 30 minutes.
- p99 regression > 20% over 30 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx + timeouts) increase > 0.2% absolute over 30 minutes, or sustained > 2x baseline.
- Streaming cadence: inter-token gap p95 regression > 10% sustained for 30 minutes.
- Queue delay p95 exceeds tier guardrail for > 15 minutes (guardrail values to be confirmed per tier).

Acceptance criteria
- Documented backlog of tuning changes with owners, scope (model family + GPU SKU), and gating metrics.
- Model registry contains initial set of tier overrides for (at minimum) H100, A100, L40S (and any SKU implicated by beta incidents).
- Perf canary covers the expanded matrix and blocks merges on agreed thresholds.
- A written expansion plan with ramp schedule per region and clear rollback decision owners.
- Support-facing troubleshooting notes updated (tie-off with INT-3301; at minimum include: how to view effective config, how to interpret queue delay, and when to switch tiers).

Notes
- Keep backwards compatibility: explicit batching knobs must continue to override tier defaults. Ensure “effective config” clearly indicates precedence and where each value came from.
- Coordinate with SRE on alert noise: we had early false positives on queue delay alerts; thresholds need to be tier-aware and use burn-rate style windows where possible.

Proposed sub-issue breakdown (to be created / tracked under this)
- ENG-18601: Add streaming cadence p95 metric + canary gate for fast tier
- ENG-18602: SKU-specific KV cache pressure defaults for cost-efficient tier (L40S/A10/L4)
- ENG-18603: Long-context override rules + admission control tuning
- ENG-18604: Expand perf canary model/SKU matrix for Phase 2 models
- ENG-18605: Region expansion runbook + rollout config templates
- ENG-18606: Dashboard updates: split server queue delay vs network variance indicators
- ENG-18607: Effective config logging standard (runtime + console) for tier/override debugging
- ENG-18608: CS/SE troubleshooting playbook updates (handoff with INT-3301)
comments: 2025-03-19 (Rafael Mendes): Please align abort thresholds with the tier SLO doc; queue delay alerts were too noisy in beta—recommend burn-rate windows rather than static thresholds.

2025-03-22 (Jonas Weber): For Phase 2 model expansion, we should require quality gate re-run only if tier mapping changes materially (not just registry overrides). Suggest we tag overrides that are 'perf-only' vs 'behavioral'.
2025-03-27 (Omar El-Sayed): Reproduced SUP-18492-like timeouts on L40S with cost-efficient at conc=32; likely KV cache budget. I can draft SKU overrides this week if we agree on the cap strategy.

2025-04-01 (Sofia Ivanova): Agree on prioritizing streaming cadence metric + canary gate first. Once we have that, we can safely re-open fast-tier queue delay tuning without risking a repeat of PR 18463 regression.
